content.title: Recommendations for management of ventricular arrhythmias and bradyarrhythmias

ventricular_arrhythmias.indication: Patients with polymorphic VT and/or VF unless contraindicated
Myocardial ischaemia in patients with recurrent VT and/or VF

ventricular_arrhythmias.recommendation: Transvenous catheter pacing termination and/or overdrive pacing
ventricular_arrhythmias.indication: If VT cannot be controlled by repeated electrical cardioversion

ventricular_arrhythmias.recommendation: Radiofrequency catheter ablation at a specialized ablation centre followed by ICD implantation
ventricular_arrhythmias.indication: Patients with recurrent VT, VF, or electrical storm despite complete revascularization and optimal medical therapy
Recurrent VT with haemodynamic relevance when beta-blockers, amiodarone, and overdrive stimulation are not effective/applicable

ventricular_arrhythmias.recommendation: Sedation or general anaesthesia to reduce sympathetic drive
ventricular_arrhythmias.indication: Patients with recurrent life-threatening ventricular arrhythmias

ventricular_arrhythmias.recommendation: ICD implantation or temporary use of a wearable cardioverter defibrillator
ventricular_arrhythmias.indication: <40 days after MI in selected patients (incomplete revascularization, pre-existing LVEF dysfunction, arrhythmias >48 h after STEMI onset, polymorphic VT or VF)

ventricular_arrhythmias.recommendation: Do not treat asymptomatic and haemodynamically irrelevant ventricular arrhythmias with anti-arrhythmic drugs
ventricular_arrhythmias.indication: Asymptomatic and haemodynamically irrelevant ventricular arrhythmias

bradyarrhythmias.general: In cases of sinus bradycardia with haemodynamic intolerance or high-degree AV block without stable escape rhythm

content.notes: Guideline excerpt includes recommendation classes (I, IIa, IIb, III) and evidence grades (B, C). Mentions clinical situations related to MI/STEMI, LVEF dysfunction, polymorphic VT/VF, electrical storm, and use of ICD/wearable defibrillators.
